name: Rezūm II
question: Does transurethral convective water vapor thermal therapy relieve BPH-related lower urinary tract symptoms more than a sham procedure?

arms.label: sham rigid cystoscopy with simulated treatment sounds

design.population: Men aged 50 or older with IPSS 13 or higher, peak flow rate 15 mL/s or less and prostate volume 30–80 cc, with or without a median lobe.
design.locator: Abstract (J Urol 2016); final 5-year report journal pp717–719 and Figure 1; ClinicalTrials.gov NCT01912339 results

verdictNote: Sham-controlled at 3 months only; durability data are uncontrolled treatment-arm follow-up to 5 years.
takeaway: In 197 men with BPH symptoms and 30–80 cc prostates, convective water vapor thermal therapy (Rezūm) reduced IPSS by 11.2 points versus 4.3 with sham rigid cystoscopy at 3 months (p < 0.0001); controls then crossed over, and no de novo erectile dysfunction was reported.

reports.label: Initial randomized report
reports.dateLocator: PubMed entry date; accepted 2015-11-03; print issue May 2016
reports.citation: McVary KT, Gange SN, Gittelman MC, et al. Minimally invasive prostate convective water vapor energy ablation: a multicenter, randomized, controlled study for the treatment of lower urinary tract symptoms secondary to benign prostatic hyperplasia. *J Urol.* 2016;195(5):1529-1538. doi:10.1016/j.juro.2015.10.181
reports.followUp: 3-month randomized comparison; treatment arm followed to 12 months

results.measure: Change in IPSS from baseline at 3 months (mean ± SD; mean difference is treatment minus sham)
results.note: The prespecified hypothesis was that the IPSS reduction with treatment exceeds 125% of the reduction with sham (final 5-year report, journal p718). The mean difference and its interval are the Cochrane review's calculation in 195 men with efficacy data; the ClinicalTrials.gov record gives 95% CIs of −12.5 to −9.9 and −6.1 to −2.5 for the two group means in the intention-to-treat population (136 and 61).
results.locator: Abstract; ClinicalTrials.gov NCT01912339 results, primary outcome 1; Kang 2020 Cochrane review, Analysis 1.1

results.measure: Composite at 3 months: new severe retention lasting more than 21 days, rectourethral fistula, or rectal or gastrointestinal perforation (treatment arm only)
results.note: Prespecified performance goal: 12% or less. The registry gives a 95% CI of 0–4.6%.
results.locator: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT01912339 results, primary outcome 2; FDA 510(k) K150786 summary, section 1.10.3

results.measure: 30% or greater IPSS reduction from baseline at 3 months
results.note: Responder counts at 6 and 12 months in the treatment arm were 102/136 and 104/136 (registry).

results.measure: Treatment-arm mean IPSS at 2 weeks (baseline 22)
results.note: The treatment-arm IPSS fell by 50% or more from baseline at 3, 6 and 12 months (p < 0.0001).

results.measure: Treatment-arm change in peak flow rate at 3 months
results.note: Sustained through 12 months (p < 0.0001). The abstract gives no sham comparison for this endpoint.

harms.label: Clavien–Dindo grade III–V adverse events
harms.note: Risk ratio 6.79 (95% CI 0.39–117.00), very low-certainty evidence.

harms.label: Clavien–Dindo grade I–II adverse events
harms.note: Risk ratio 1.89 (95% CI 1.15–3.11) for treatment versus sham, low-certainty evidence; examples were dysuria, hematuria, frequency, urgency, hematospermia and urinary infection. The primary report describes adverse events as mild to moderate and quickly resolved.

harms.label: Catheterization before discharge
harms.locator: Boston Scientific Rezūm directions for use (Canada, 2021), Table 5
harms.note: Mean catheter duration 3.4 ± 3.2 days (N = 123; median 2.9, range 0.0–30.9) versus 0.9 ± 0.8 days (N = 12). Of the 122 treated men catheterized, 83 (68%) were catheterized at physician discretion. The Cochrane review gives a risk ratio of 35.58 (95% CI 15.37–82.36) for an indwelling catheter.

reports.followUp: 5 years: 77 of 135 treated men (57%) and 21 of 53 crossover men evaluated at 60 months

results.measure: Treatment-arm mean IPSS change from baseline (22.0) at 5 years, per-protocol
results.note: Reported as a reduction of near 48%; IPSS was 10.6 at 3 months (change −11.3 ± 7.6).

results.measure: Treatment-arm mean IPSS quality-of-life score at 5 years (baseline 4.4 ± 1.1)
results.note: Reported as a 45% reduction; 2.3 ± 1.5 at 3 months.

results.measure: Treatment-arm mean peak flow rate at 5 years (baseline 9.9 ± 2.2 mL/s)
results.note: The text reports 49% improvement; the abstract reports 44%. Flow was 15.5 ± 6.7 mL/s at 1 year.

results.measure: Treatment-arm mean BPH Impact Index at 5 years
results.note: The text reports a 45% decline at 5 years after a peak decrease of 51% at 6 months (2.1 ± 1.5); the abstract reports 48%.

results.measure: Cumulative surgical retreatment through 5 years, treatment arm
results.note: Cumulative surgical retreatment was 2.2% at 12 months, 3.7% at 24 months and 4.4% from 36 months. Of the 6 men, 4 had obstructive median tissue left untreated; 83% of surgical retreatments occurred in the first 2 years and none after year 3. BPH medication was started by a further 11.1% through 5 years (0.8% at 12 months).

results.measure: Retreatment through 5 years in the 53 crossover men
results.note: Three of the 4 surgical retreatments were for previously untreated obstructive median tissue.

results.measure: Treatment-arm men both free from retreatment and with a 30% or greater IPSS reduction at 5 years
Change in IIEF erectile function and MSHQ-EjD function domains at 5 years, treatment arm
results.note: The authors attribute the modest changes to aging of the cohort. No device- or procedure-related de novo erectile dysfunction occurred; the MSHQ-EjD bother score improved 16% at 60 months.

harms.label: Dysuria
harms.note: Device- or procedure-related, treatment arm; 18.9% in the crossover group. Mild to moderate, resolved spontaneously or with routine treatment.

harms.label: Hematospermia
harms.note: 3.8% in the crossover group. Urinary frequency 5.9% and 5.7%.

harms.label: Related adverse events overall
harms.value: 151 events in 53 treatment-arm men; 59 events in 23 crossover men
harms.note: No late related adverse events occurred in years 1 to 5, and no withdrawal was attributed to a device- or procedure-related event.
